title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a role of trees and plants? (1 mark)
   A. They give oxygen and shade
   B. They make the sun set
   C. They dry up rivers
   D. They stop rain forever

2. Where did Prince Siddhartha sit under the Bodhi tree? (1 mark)
   A. Amritsar
   B. Bodh Gaya
   C. Nairobi
   D. Lumbini

3. Which two elements are needed for a crop to grow well? (1 mark)
   A. Water and earth
   B. Space and salt
   C. Fire and metal
   D. Metal and stone

4. Which of these is one of the five great elements? (1 mark)
   A. Akash
   B. Wood
   C. Metal
   D. Salt

5. What should we never throw into rivers? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic and waste
   B. Clean leaves
   C. Rain
   D. Rainwater

6. The soil in a shamba belongs to which element? (1 mark)
   A. Akash
   B. Prithvi
   C. Vayu
   D. Agni

7. Which of these is NOT one of the five elements? (1 mark)
   A. Vayu
   B. Prithvi
   C. Agni
   D. Metal

8. What do all four Enlightened Beings in the lesson teach in common? (1 mark)
   A. Anger
   B. Selfishness
   C. Pride
   D. Kindness, truth and service

9. Where is Lumbini today? (1 mark)
   A. In Kenya
   B. In Nepal
   C. In Punjab
   D. In Uganda

10. What does the word Enlightened mean in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Very tall
   B. Very rich
   C. Full of the light of true knowledge
   D. Very loud

11. Who was Prahlad? (1 mark)
   A. A Jain monk
   B. The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   C. A Sikh Guru
   D. A river

12. What is a Tirthankar in Jainism? (1 mark)
   A. A temple
   B. A festival
   C. A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   D. A king

13. Which activity helps us remember the teachings of Enlightened Beings? (1 mark)
   A. Acting a skit of a story
   B. Reading it silently
   C. Colouring the poster
   D. Reading the story aloud twice

14. Who was Hiranyakashipu? (1 mark)
   A. A proud and cruel king
   B. A river
   C. A good teacher
   D. A festival

15. During which Jain festival is the Kalpasutra often read? (1 mark)
   A. Madaraka Day
   B. Maha Shivratri
   C. Paryushan
   D. Vasant Panchami

16. What is a scripture? (1 mark)
   A. A type of food
   B. A kind of festival
   C. A holy book with teachings
   D. A musical instrument

17. Who went into the forest with Ram? (1 mark)
   A. Sita and Lakshman
   B. Vishwamitra
   C. Kaikeyi
   D. Bharat and Shatrughna

18. Which faith does the Dhammapada belong to? (1 mark)
   A. Hinduism
   B. Sikhism
   C. Jainism
   D. Buddhism

19. When can Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva be said? (1 mark)
   A. Only at a wedding
   B. Never
   C. Only at a funeral
   D. Before meals and in the evening

20. What are bhajans? (1 mark)
   A. Devotional songs
   B. Sports
   C. Exams
   D. Maps

21. Which prayer starts with the words Twameva mata cha pita twameva? (1 mark)
   A. Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva
   B. Saraswati Vandana
   C. Gayatri Mantra
   D. Om Namah Shivaya

22. In which Kenyan towns are Mandirs found? (1 mark)
   A. Only Lamu
   B. None
   C. Only in villages
   D. Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu

23. What is the garbhagriha? (1 mark)
   A. The car park
   B. The gate
   C. The kitchen
   D. The inner room where the murti is placed

24. What does mata mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Mother
   B. Teacher
   C. Friend
   D. Father

25. What is a parable? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A short story with a lesson
   C. A kind of prayer
   D. A festival

26. In Sasankasana, where do you rest your forehead? (1 mark)
   A. On your knees
   B. On a chair
   C. On the wall
   D. On the mat

27. Which is a benefit of yoga? (1 mark)
   A. It helps us breathe well and stay calm
   B. It gives instant riches
   C. It makes us noisy
   D. It stops rain

28. Which organisation set International Yoga Day? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A bank
   C. A local school
   D. The United Nations

29. Which pose do you start Sasankasana from? (1 mark)
   A. Vajra Asana
   B. Lying down
   C. Standing
   D. A handstand

30. How does Namaste show the idea of Paramatma? (1 mark)
   A. It means goodbye only
   B. It shows respect for the divine in everyone
   C. It is a race
   D. It is a food

31. What does the Shibi story teach? (1 mark)
   A. Kings do not care
   B. Hawks always win
   C. A kind person protects the weak
   D. Doves are bad

32. Which tradition teaches the five principles in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Only the Buddhist tradition
   B. A market
   C. A trade union
   D. Sanatan or Vedic

33. Why is prayer a principle of Dharma? (1 mark)
   A. It builds houses
   B. It makes us proud
   C. It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   D. It ends homework

34. Who became the first Prime Minister of Kenya at that time? (1 mark)
   A. Jomo Kenyatta
   B. Mwai Kibaki
   C. Daniel arap Moi
   D. Tom Mboya

35. Paryushan Parva is a festival of which faith? (1 mark)
   A. Sikhism
   B. Jainism
   C. Buddhism
   D. Hinduism

36. How should you behave when visiting a friend's festival? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at customs
   B. Shout
   C. Refuse to take part
   D. Listen and ask polite questions

37. How long is Paryushan in one Jain tradition? (1 mark)
   A. Two days
   B. One year
   C. One month
   D. Eight days

38. Guru (Brihaspati) is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Venus
   B. Saturn
   C. Jupiter
   D. Mars

39. What is the Indian name for Monday? (1 mark)
   A. Guruvaar
   B. Ravivaar
   C. Budhvaar
   D. Somvaar

40. Which of these is a month of the Indian traditional calendar? (1 mark)
   A. January
   B. March
   C. Chaitra
   D. June

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should we not bully others, according to the teachings in this lesson? (2 marks)

42. Give four roles of sacred plants. (4 marks)

43. List three things you should do before starting yoga. (3 marks)

44. Why should we visit a friend's festival respectfully? (3 marks)

45. Draw and label a simple Mandir. Name four features you would show. (4 marks)

46. Describe the lessons of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra. (4 marks)

47. Explain what Hindus mean by an Avtar. (2 marks)

48. Name the months of the Indian traditional calendar in which Maha Shivratri and Paryushan fall. (3 marks)

49. Describe the day of prayers for a child. (5 marks)

50. Write the seven days of the week in the Indian traditional calendar with their heavenly bodies. (4 marks)

51. Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya. (5 marks)

52. Write three signs of integrity at school. (3 marks)

53. What is a rite or ritual? Give one example. (2 marks)

54. Match four scriptures with their faiths. (4 marks)

55. State three rules of good behaviour when visiting a Mandir. (3 marks)

56. Explain why balance is important in the four Purusharthas. (5 marks)

57. Explain the words Micchami Dukkadam said at Paryushan. (2 marks)

58. What does yoga mean? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — They give oxygen and shade
   Plants clean the air and give shade.

2. B — Bodh Gaya
   He became the Buddha at Bodh Gaya.

3. A — Water and earth
   Soil and water help a crop to grow.

4. A — Akash
   The five elements are Prithvi, Jal, Agni, Vayu and Akash.

5. A — Plastic and waste
   Waste harms water and living things.

6. B — Prithvi
   Soil is earth, or Prithvi.

7. D — Metal
   The five are earth, water, fire, air and space.

8. D — Kindness, truth and service
   Their teachings are alike in these values.

9. B — In Nepal
   Lumbini lies in Nepal.

10. C — Full of the light of true knowledge
   Enlightened beings are wise and full of true knowledge.

11. B — The young son of Hiranyakashipu who loved Vishnu
   Prahlad stayed faithful to Vishnu.

12. C — A teacher who shows the path across the river of life
   Tirthankars guide people to freedom.

13. A — Acting a skit of a story
   A skit helps us learn the lesson.

14. A — A proud and cruel king
   He was Prahlad's proud father.

15. C — Paryushan
   Many Jains listen to it during Paryushan.

16. C — A holy book with teachings
   Scriptures hold the wisdom of great teachers.

17. A — Sita and Lakshman
   Sita and Lakshman chose to go with him.

18. D — Buddhism
   It is a collection of Buddhist verses.

19. D — Before meals and in the evening
   It is said before meals, at assembly and in the evening.

20. A — Devotional songs
   Bhajans are songs of prayer.

21. A — Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva
   It begins with these words.

22. D — Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu
   Mandirs are found in many Kenyan towns.

23. D — The inner room where the murti is placed
   It is the inner sanctum.

24. A — Mother
   Mata means mother and pita means father.

25. B — A short story with a lesson
   A parable teaches a moral.

26. D — On the mat
   The forehead rests on the mat.

27. A — It helps us breathe well and stay calm
   Yoga calms the body and mind.

28. D — The United Nations
   The UN chose the day in 2014.

29. A — Vajra Asana
   You start sitting on heels.

30. B — It shows respect for the divine in everyone
   Namaste honours the divine in others.

31. C — A kind person protects the weak
   Kindness protects the weak.

32. D — Sanatan or Vedic
   It is the ancient Hindu way.

33. C — It makes us thankful, calm and humble
   Prayer helps us feel calm.

34. A — Jomo Kenyatta
   Jomo Kenyatta was the first Prime Minister.

35. B — Jainism
   It is the main Jain festival.

36. D — Listen and ask polite questions
   Respect is key.

37. D — Eight days
   Eight days in one tradition and ten in another.

38. C — Jupiter
   Guru is Jupiter.

39. D — Somvaar
   Som is the Moon.

40. C — Chaitra
   Chaitra is the first month.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Enlightened Beings teach kindness and Ahimsa, so we should not harm others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for kindness or Ahimsa, 1 mark for a link to bullying.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen and clean the air; they give shade for rest and prayer; their leaves, fruits and bark are used for food and medicine; their leaves and flowers are used in worship; they remind us to care for life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct role.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear loose clothes, prepare a mat, have an empty stomach, find a quiet place, meet with a teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: We listen, ask polite questions, do not laugh at customs, and build peace among communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: A hall, a spire, a door with steps, a bell or flag, and the murti room (any four labelled).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct feature labelled.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Practise Ahimsa, be honest, control greed and anger, and respect teachers (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form in which God is believed to come to earth to protect goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for God coming to earth and 1 mark for protecting goodness.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Maha Shivratri in Phalguna and Paryushan in Bhadrapada.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each and 1 mark for correct spelling.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: In the morning, the Gayatri Mantra and the Saraswati Vandana before study; at midday before meals, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva; in the evening, thanks to God. Also sit calmly and fold hands.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part of the day, 1 mark for manners.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ravivaar: Sun; Somvaar: Moon; Mangalvaar: Mars; Budhvaar: Mercury; Guruvaar: Jupiter; Shukravaar: Venus; Shanivaar: Saturn.
   Working / marking points: Award 1 mark for every two correct pairs, up to 4.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Not cheating, owning up to mistakes, handing in lost items, telling the truth, doing your own work (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: A special action done in a set way at a festival, such as lighting a lamp or raising a flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ramayan: Hinduism. Kalpasutra: Jainism. Dhammapada: Buddhism. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji: Sikhism.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Remove shoes, dress modestly, speak softly, switch off phones, do not touch the murti, ask before taking photographs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wealth and wishes are good but must follow Dharma. Without balance, chasing money or wishes can lead to cheating and harm, while Dharma keeps us honest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for balance, 2 marks for Dharma guiding the others, 2 marks for an example.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: May any harm I did in thought, word or deed be forgiven.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for forgiveness.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: To join or unite the body, breath and mind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for join, 1 mark for the three things.
